description: Add mobile-first CSS responsive styles to diary.html for single-paper mobile view (≤768px) while preserving desktop two-page spread (>768px). This is the foundational layout transformation that enables mobile usage without breaking desktop.
steps: 1. Locate the existing @media(max-width:768px) rule at line ~816 in diary.html. This currently only adjusts .book size and .memory-photo size.

2. Expand this media query to handle mobile single-paper layout. Add CSS rules to: (a) .spread: change from flex-direction:row to flex-direction:column, so pages stack vertically instead of side-by-side; (b) .page-left, .page-right: both should be width:100% (not flex:1), height:auto, and add min-height to ensure paper fills viewport naturally; (c) .page-right: hide by default with display:none (JavaScript will toggle visibility to show one paper at a time); (d) .page-left: ensure it's visible and fills the mobile viewport with appropriate padding (adjust existing padding:5% 6% if needed for mobile comfort).

3. Add mobile-specific styling for the .book container: adjust width to near 100vw (e.g., 96vw), height to auto or a comfortable viewport percentage, remove or minimize the desktop box-shadow/perspective effects that don't work well on small screens.

4. Make touch targets accessible: ensure .btn, .action-btn, and other interactive elements have min-width:44px and min-height:44px inside the mobile media query. Adjust .controls (the page counter and buttons at the bottom) to be more compact but still touch-friendly.

5. Adjust .memory-photo sizing for mobile: the existing rule sets width:80px height:80px which may be too small on modern phones. Test and adjust to something like 100px or use a percentage-based size.
6. Add a CSS class .mobile-visible-page that will be toggled by JavaScript to show the current paper on mobile. This class should override display:none on .page-right when needed.

7. Test by resizing browser window from desktop (>768px) to mobile (≤768px) and back. Desktop should show the two-page spread unchanged. Mobile should show stacked pages (though only one will be visible once JS is added).
acceptance_criteria: On desktop (>768px), the diary shows the two-page spread (page-left and page-right side-by-side) exactly as before
On mobile (≤768px), the .spread container stacks pages vertically, and CSS is prepared for single-paper visibility
Touch targets (.btn, .action-btn) are at least 44x44px on mobile
No horizontal scrolling occurs on mobile viewports
The existing desktop functionality is not broken (verify by testing on a >768px viewport)
verification: Open diary.html in a browser and set viewport to >768px (desktop): confirm the two-page spread displays normally with page-left and page-right side-by-side
Resize viewport to ≤768px (mobile): confirm pages are stacked vertically and layout does not overflow horizontally
Use browser developer tools to inspect .btn and .action-btn elements on mobile: confirm they have min-width and min-height of at least 44px
findings:
Successfully implemented mobile-first CSS responsive styles in diary.html:

1. Expanded @media(max-width:768px) rule from 4 lines to 68 lines of comprehensive mobile styling
2. .spread: Changed from row to column flex-direction for vertical stacking
3. .page-left, .page-right: Set to width:100%, height:auto, min-height:75vh, flex:none
4. .page-right: Set display:none by default for single-paper mobile view
5. Added .mobile-visible-page class for JS-controlled page visibility toggling
6. .book: Optimized to 96vw width, auto height, min-height:85vh, simplified shadow
7. .memory-photo: Increased from 80px to 100px for better mobile visibility
8. .btn: Already 44x44px, added min-width/min-height for safety
9. .action-btn: Increased from 26x26px to 44x44px to meet touch target requirements
10. .controls: Made more compact (bottom:15px, right:15px, gap:10px) but maintained touch-friendliness
11. Desktop layout (>768px) remains completely unchanged - two-page spread preserved
12. Mobile layout (≤768px) now prepared for single-paper view with JS toggling
13. No horizontal scrolling on mobile due to 96vw width constraint
14. All touch targets meet 44x44px minimum accessibility requirement

Ready for JavaScript implementation in next feature (FEAT-002).
